notesDetails.title: Seatbelt 'proxy_only' Sandbox Blocked Loopback TCP (:eperm) & PTYs — Masking 16 Host Test Failures (81/97 Passed)
bullets: Why Only 68/97 Tests Ran Inside the Session: Muse Code launched with security_mode: {approval: "disabled", sandbox: "normal"} and local_command_network: {mode: "proxy_only"} (session.jsonl lines 1 & 9). Under macOS Seatbelt, every :gen_tcp.listen(0, ...) call failed with {:error, :eperm} (and Mix's TCP concurrency lock required MIX_OS_CONCURRENCY_LOCK=0 on every command). When the agent attempted an unsandboxed bash call on Turn 13 (events.jsonl line 234), the harness rejected it ("unsandboxed execution requires human approval, but approval prompts are disabled"). The agent wrote 68 pure/closed-port tests that passed in-sandbox and 29 local-TCP tests that it marked 'verified by inspection for CI' in PLAN.md.

Forensic Breakdown of All 16 Host Test Failures (81/97 Passed in 114.8s): Running mix test outside the sandbox executes the 29 server-backed tests; 13 pass (81/97 total) and 16 fail across 5 unverified code/test bugs: (1) 7 failures in test/capy_bench/http/conn_test.exs (lines 16–64): setup returns {:ok, server: server}, but all 7 test heads pattern-match %{port: port}, raising FunctionClauseError once TestServer.start!() succeeds; (2) 2 failures in test/capy_bench/cli_interrupt_test.exs (lines 79 & 105): the Python wrapper calls os.setsid() inside Port.open, which raises PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted because OTP 28's erl_child_setup already makes the port child a process-group leader; (3) 4 failures in test/capy_bench/cli_http_test.exs (lines 181, 194, 210, 235): assert_summary/5 line 51 matches ~r/^Latency \(HTTP responses\): p50 (\d+|n\/a) ms, p95 (\d+|n\/a) ms$/, but CapyBench.Report prints "p50 n/a, p95 n/a" without " ms" when 0 responses complete; (4) 2 failures in HTTPS negative tests (cli_http_test.exs lines 154 & 168): OTP's default :logger prints TLS client Fatal - Bad Certificate / Unknown CA notices to stdout (breaking the 6-line summary parser) AND TestServer.accept_loop/5 (test_server.ex:115) crashes with CaseClauseError on {:error, {:tls_alert, ...}}; and (5) 1 failure in cli_http_test.exs:121 (latency includes connection setup): TestServer.accept_loop sleeps accept_delay_ms: 100 in userspace while the OS kernel TCP listen backlog completes the 3-way handshake immediately in parallel with the client's 100ms pacing interval.

notesDetails.title: Why S7 Failed in Real Foreground Terminals: Background '&' SIG_IGN Misdiagnosis & Port Process-Group Isolation
bullets: Note vs. Repo PLAN.md on S7 (6/7 Holdout vs. 7/7 Checked): Although the agent checked [x] on S1–S7 in PLAN.md and committed 778d88e ('S7: handle Ctrl-C with partial summary and exit 130'), both S7 e2e tests in test/capy_bench/cli_interrupt_test.exs fail and pressing Ctrl-C against ./cb in a real foreground PTY kills the process immediately with return code -2 (SIGINT) and '^C' (zero summary output on stdout), matching the manual note's [ ] S7 assessment.

How the S1 Sandbox Probe Misdiagnosed Escript SIGINT Behavior (Turns 41–68): When pty.fork() failed in Turn 58 with OSError: out of pty devices (blocked by Seatbelt), the agent tested SIGINT in Turns 41, 62, and 63 via non-interactive bash scripts (/tmp/probe/sigtest.sh, /tmp/probe/sigmatrix.sh) that started the escript in the background with '&' ("$1" hello > /tmp/probe/out.log 2>&1 &). Because POSIX shells without job control automatically set SIGINT to SIG_IGN for background '&' jobs, kill -INT $PID had no effect—leading the agent to falsely conclude in PLAN.md line 42 that 'an escript-mode BEAM ignores SIGINT' and omit +Bi or a wrapper script.

Why CapyBench.Interrupt's /bin/sh Port Never Sees Terminal Ctrl-C: Based on that false premise, lib/capy_bench/interrupt.ex spawns Port.open({:spawn_executable, "/bin/sh"}, [{:args, ["-c", "trap 'printf \"INTERRUPTED\\n\"' INT; read -r line || exit 0"]}, ...]). Because BEAM's erl_child_setup calls setsid()/setpgid(0, 0) on spawned port children, the /bin/sh helper runs in its own isolated process group and never receives terminal process-group SIGINT; it only passed unit test test/capy_bench/interrupt_test.exs because line 11 sent kill -INT directly to the helper's OS PID.

notesDetails.title: Mid-Turn Async Context Compaction at 384k Tokens (Turn 339): Why the Final Summary Claimed S1–S7 Were 'Already Implemented'
bullets: Crossing the 384,000-Token Soft Compaction Threshold (Turns 334–338): During the post-S7 release review pass, prompt context crossed Muse Code's soft_threshold_tokens: 384000 on Turn 334 (384,396 prompt tokens at 16:43:39 WIB), triggering background compaction candidate-3982 (strategy_id: "summary-preserved-suffix/v1", session.jsonl line 10297). While the async summarizer ran for 29.4 seconds, the agent executed Turns 335–338, reaching a peak of 388,500 prompt tokens (388,832 total tokens, 38.54% of the 1,007,997 context limit) on Turn 338.

88.9% Context Drop on Turn 339 & Post-Compaction Persona Shift: At 16:44:08 WIB (session.jsonl line 10444), install-4043 replaced all conversation history through sequence 3967 (Turns 1–331, covering S1–S7 implementation) with a structured markdown handoff summary, dropping Turn 339's prompt from 388,500 tokens to 39,249 uncached tokens. Because the post-compaction context began from that summary, the agent's final response (events.jsonl line 6639) reported: 'Done: S1–S7 were already implemented; this session finished with a review consolidation pass plus release verification, committed as 510b20e.'

notesDetails.title: 8.5x Larger Initial Harness Prompt vs. Pi (29.2k vs. 3.4k Tokens) & Custom AST Lint Gate (mix capy_bench.lint)
bullets: Harness Ablation — Muse Code vs. Pi on muse-spark-1.3-contributor: On Turn 1, Muse Code v1.4.14 sent 85,375 bytes (29,181 input tokens: 48,581 bytes of base instructions + 36,397 bytes of developer context blocks including a 20,739-byte skills catalog for Blender, Web3D/WGSL, and workflow authoring, plus 397 bytes of user prompt), compared to just 3,437 tokens on Pi. Combined with 358 vs. 239 turns, Muse Code consumed 2.49x more total tokens (74.07M vs. 29.74M) and 78.6% higher cost ($0.25 vs. $0.14).

Custom Elixir AST Linter (lib/mix/tasks/capy_bench/lint.ex) & Silent Crash Dumps: Because the sandbox blocked Hex package fetches in S1 (Turns 10–11 & 80–82), the agent built a 122-line custom Mix task (mix capy_bench.lint) using Code.string_to_quoted/2 and Macro.prewalk/2 to enforce @moduledoc presence, ban debug calls (IO.inspect/2, dbg/1, IEx.pry/0), and reject TODO/FIXME markers across all 10 lib/ files. However, piping mix commands through '| head' repeatedly closed stdout early on the BEAM, generating erl_crash.dump files that required prepending 'rm -f erl_crash.dump;' to every git add command from S2 through S7.
